1.0: QUESTION: What is the fundamental nature of mathematical objects - are they discovered platonic entities or human inventions?
1.1: ASSERTS: Platonist position - mathematical truths exist necessarily and independently of human minds
1.2: ASSERTS: Constructivist/formalist position - mathematics is a human artifact shaped by social practice
1.3: DOCUMENT: Most working mathematicians are informal platonists in practice - they speak of finding proofs, not inventing them
1.4: DOCUMENT: Many philosophers favor constructivist or structuralist accounts that avoid metaphysical commitments to abstract realms
1.5: OPEN: The question of mathematical ontology remains genuinely unresolved
1.1.1: ASSERTS: Mathematical facts like 2 + 2 = 4 do not depend on human minds
1.1.2: ASSERTS: We discover rather than invent mathematical objects such as prime numbers
1.1.3: ASSERTS: Mathematical objects inhabit a realm of abstract forms to which we have epistemic access
1.1.4: ASSERTS: Platonism explains mathematics' apparent objectivity
1.1.5: ASSERTS: Platonism explains the unreasonable effectiveness of mathematics in physics
1.1.6: ASSERTS: Platonism explains the sense of constraint mathematicians feel - they cannot arbitrarily declare theorems false
1.1.7: REJECTS: Platonism struggles to explain how physical beings access an abstract realm
1.1.8: REJECTS: Platonism struggles to explain why the abstract realm contains exactly the structures useful to physics
1.2.1: ASSERTS: Mathematics is a rule-governed symbol game
1.2.2: ASSERTS: Mathematics is a social practice shaped by history, notation, and shared convention
1.2.3: ASSERTS: Different cultures developed different mathematical systems
1.2.4: ASSERTS: Axiom choice matters, indicating mathematics is not purely discovered
1.2.5: ASSERTS: Foundations crises were genuine disputes rather than revelations of preexisting fact
1.2.6: ASSERTS: Mathematics feels necessary because we are trained into its practices
1.2.7: REJECTS: Constructivism struggles to explain why mathematical results feel discovered
1.2.8: REJECTS: Constructivism struggles to explain why mathematics resists our preferences
1.2.9: REJECTS: Constructivism struggles to explain why mathematics works so well in describing the physical world
